---
title: "Compatibility with CmdStanR"
---

CmdStanPHP ports CmdStanR's model, executable, and CSV workflow to PHP. It does not implement every CmdStanR feature. The reference is CmdStanR 1.0 (its release candidate, from the v1.0 branch), with the [CmdStanR API](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/reference/) and the [CmdStan command-line options](https://mc-stan.org/docs/cmdstan-guide/command_line_options.html).

## Supported {#supported-workflows}

| CmdStanR capability | PHP implementation | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installation path/version (CmdStan 2.37 or newer), source/JSON writing | Namespaced functions | Unit tests, local version detection; installer build is a CI step |
| Installation from a release URL or local tarball, overwrite, `make/local`, copying `make/local` from the current installation | `install_cmdstan()`, `cmdstan_make_local()` | Offline tests with generated tarballs; network downloads are exercised only by CI's official-release install |
| Model construction and compilation | `CmdStanModel`, `cmdstan_model()`, `compile_stan_file()` | Real C++ builds |
| Build records, recompilation when the program, includes, user header, options, `make/local`, or CmdStan change, and stale-executable checks | `.<exe>.cmdstanphp.json`, `isCurrent()`, `buildInfo()`, `stan_build_info()`, `StaleExecutableException` | Unit tests with a stand-in CmdStan, including rebuilds and a failed build; real C++ builds |

## Naming {#method-names}

- Methods are camelCase, as PSR-1 requires, with no snake_case alias: CmdStanR's `fit$output_files()` is `$fit->outputFiles()`.
- Standalone functions, option names, CSV metadata keys, result-array keys, and summary measure names keep CmdStanR's spelling, as in `sample(iter_warmup: 500)` and `Summary::summarise($draws, ['ess_bulk'])`.
- A matching name does not imply matching behavior. [Differences](#php-adaptations) describes behavior.

## Differences {#php-adaptations}

### Data

- R named lists become associative PHP arrays, and numeric arrays must be rectangular lists. Complex numbers are `[re, im]` pairs, and tuples are lists of their elements.
- R sparse matrices, `NA`, and automatic R object conversion have no PHP equivalent.
- Data frames and factors can come from phibble or any object with `toModelData()` or `toColumns()`, as described in [Data frames](api-data-frames.qmd). Table data with string columns is refused, as in CmdStanR 1.0.
- `code()` returns one source string. Syntax errors throw exceptions instead of returning an R diagnostic list.

### Draws and summaries

- Draws are PHP arrays with documented shapes. Indices are zero-based, and draw metadata is one-based. R's tibble, posterior, bayesplot, and ggplot2 classes are not emulated. [Draws, summaries, and saving fits](draws.qmd) describes the formats.
- Summary quantiles use linear interpolation (R's default type 7), and scaled MAD uses 1.4826.
- The default MCMC summary takes R-hat and bulk ESS from the installed CmdStan's `stansummary` and computes tail ESS in PHP. With `measures`, `summary()` uses a PHP port of posterior's `summarise_draws()` and needs no CmdStan. Results are checked against the installed R packages and are not guaranteed to be identical to every posterior version.
- ADVI's mean row is stored separately. ADVI and Laplace `log_p__` columns become `lp__`, and their approximate densities `lp_approx__`, as in CmdStanR. Convergence statistics are `NAN` for fits other than MCMC.
- `metadata()` returns one merged array with CmdStanR's keys, such as `iter_sampling`, `max_treedepth`, and `stan_variable_sizes`, alongside CmdStan's raw argument names. `chainMetadata()` returns the per-chain arrays. `invMetric()` returns matrices by default and reads metric JSON when every chain has one.

### Model methods

- Model methods and exposed functions compile a shared library against the selected CmdStan and load it with PHP FFI. Web SAPIs need `ffi.enable=true` or preloading.
- Log densities drop constant terms and default to `jacobian: true`, as in CmdStanR. Unconstrained vectors are flat lists. Constrained variables are nested zero-based arrays, with matrices as lists of rows.
- Serialized fits store the library path, data, and seed, and reconnect on first use, after which the generated-quantities random number generator restarts from its seed.

### Initialization from fits

Initialization from a fit follows CmdStanR 1.0's `process_init()`. MCMC draws are resampled without replacement, an optimization estimate is repeated, and ADVI, Laplace, and Pathfinder draws are resampled with Pareto-smoothed importance weights over distinct parameter vectors. Draws that multi-path Pathfinder already resampled are not reweighted. Resampling uses PHP's seeded Mt19937 engine, so a seed selects different draws than in CmdStanR.

### Builds, processes, and files

- Concurrent builds of one model are serialized by a lock file, `.<exe>.cmdstanphp.lock`. CmdStanR has no lock, so a model built at the same moment by CmdStanR and CmdStanPHP is not protected.
- The build record is `.<exe>.cmdstanphp.json`, in CmdStanR's format 1. CmdStanR writes `.<exe>.cmdstanr.json`, so a model built by both never has one record overwritten by the other.
- Before each run, a model compares the file status (inode, size, and modification and change times) of everything the build depends on. When none changed, it skips hashing and the stanc call.
- `format()` and `format_stan_file()` return the formatted program instead of printing it.
- The progress bar is drawn on stderr, without the progressr package.
- `saveObject()` uses PHP serialization; there is no `qs2` format.
- There is no compilation spinner. `cmdstanr_spinner` is accepted and has no effect.
- `cmdstanDefaults()` names CmdStan's defaults as this package's options, and `reportedFeatures()` returns what the executable reports about its build.
- Diagnostic checks are messages from `diagnosticWarnings()`, not PHP warnings.
- Console output is printed when the processes finish. There is no R interrupt integration, and CmdStan processes still running when PHP shuts down are terminated.
- Output files are not deleted when a fit is. Saving moves files that a run created and copies imported CSV files and the data file, and existing files are never overwritten. Downstream CmdStan commands still need the CSV files of a restored fit.

### Options and defaults

- `options()` and `cmdstan_option()` provide CmdStanR's global options that have a PHP meaning. `cmdstanr_no_ver_check` and `cmdstanr_spinner` are accepted and have no effect.
- Options left `null` use CmdStan's defaults. `sample()` runs four chains, one at a time unless `parallel_chains` or `mc.cores` says otherwise. `sampleMpi()` runs one chain.
- Metric and configuration JSON are written only when requested with `save_metric`, `save_cmdstan_config`, or their options.
- The installer uses one core by default, where CmdStanR uses two.
- Pathfinder's deprecated `num_threads` raises `E_USER_DEPRECATED` and maps to `threads`. Giving both throws.
- OpenCL and MPI need external toolchains or hardware, and Windows has not been tested.

### Moment matching and loo {#moment-matching-and-loo}

Moment matching follows `loo::loo_moment_match()` as `CmdStanMCMC$loo()` calls it, with these differences from loo 2.10.1:

- The split step uses the exact inverse of the accumulated affine map T(x) = A(x − m) + m + t, which is T⁻¹(y) = A⁻¹(y − m − t) + m. loo uses A⁻¹(y − m) + m − t, which is not the inverse once a shift is combined with scaling or a covariance map.
- The split relative efficiency is the minimum over both halves of the draws. loo uses the second half twice.
- Relative efficiencies are computed from exp(log_lik − max), which avoids the `NA` that loo returns when every likelihood value is tiny.

Without the split, and with the split when only shifts are accepted, `elpd_loo` and Pareto k match loo and CmdStanR. Accepted scale and covariance steps are composed in their original order. A singular weighted covariance uses loo's identity-map fallback, keeping the mean shift and recording the reason in `covariance_fallbacks`. Other numerical or model failures stop the observation at its last accepted state and record a reason. Covariances are never regularized. The [LOO guide](loo.qmd#moment-matching) describes the result.

## Not implemented

The following CmdStanR features have no implementation:

- `expose_functions(global = TRUE)`. Functions are called as methods of the returned `StanFunctions` object. Functions ending in `_lp` and overloaded functions are listed but cannot be called.
- bayesplot's other plots, including pairs, areas, NUTS energy, and posterior predictive checks. Figures are not ggplot2 objects and cannot be extended with ggplot2 layers or themes.
- Posterior `rvar` arithmetic and R session hooks beyond the options listed above.
- Windows toolchain repair (`check_cmdstan_toolchain(fix = TRUE)`). The PHP toolchain check reports missing tools and does not install them.
- Parity with every CmdStanR version's error and warning messages.

No unsupported option is accepted silently. This repository's tests validate the implemented contract against CmdStanR 1.0 and the installed posterior and loo packages; they are not the upstream CmdStanR test suite. Direct conformance tests run CmdStanR and PHP with the same seeds and compare draws, descriptive summaries, MCMC sampler diagnostics, CSV metadata, model methods, exposed functions, PSIS, LOO, WAIC, and posterior summary measures.
